enhanced_information: Glucose-6 phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PDH) deficiency can lead to drug-induced hemolytic anemia, making G6PDH a good marker. Lactate dehydrogenase is also released from damaged red blood cells during hemolysis, suggesting it as a possible marker. Evidence supports G6PDH deficiency causing hemolytic anemia due to drugs and lactate dehydrogenase interacting with erythrocytes. Therefore, both G6PDH and lactate dehydrogenase can be considered markers of drug-induced hemolytic anemia.
